cards.explanation: The answer is that you will find it again. The Teacher says, "…after many days you will find it again." (Ecclesiastes 11:1) Notice he says many days, so this isn't a quick return. Toss it out, be patient, and keep your eyes open. I've waited on a batch to cool with less patience than that, friends.

The reason is that you don't know what disaster may come. The verse says to divide your portion "…for you do not know what disaster may befall the land." (Ecclesiastes 11:2) Seven, even eight, and he never says why those numbers. I think it's like not putting every cookie in one box, because if you drop that box, you're crying into the crumbs.

The answer is False. The Teacher says, "whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie." (Ecclesiastes 11:3) No rolling and no wind pushing it around. It lands, and there it lies.

The word is sow. "He who watches the wind will fail to sow…" (Ecclesiastes 11:4) Planting is the job, and watching the wind isn't planting. Sowing is the work that gets skipped. Meanwhile my dough has never risen from being stared at.

The answer is that he will fail to reap. The Teacher says, "…and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap." (Ecclesiastes 11:4) The man watching the wind fails to sow, and the man watching the clouds fails to reap. Sowing and reaping are the two jobs, and watching the sky doesn't get either one done.

The answer is True. The Teacher says, "As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things." (Ecclesiastes 11:5) You can't even trace the wind, so God's whole work is beyond us. I find that kind of freeing, honestly. I don't have to figure it all out to get to baking.

The word is Maker. "…the work of God, the Maker of all things." (Ecclesiastes 11:5) All things, not just some things. The Teacher puts the wind and the womb right next to it. And I live on a cookie planet made just for my baking, so I know a little about being given a place by Someone else.

The reason is that you don't know which will succeed. The Teacher says, "Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper." (Ecclesiastes 11:6) Since you can't tell which sowing will work out, you keep planting. That's why I keep stamping batch after batch, friends.

The answer is False. The Teacher says you don't know "…which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper." (Ecclesiastes 11:6) One could do well, the other could, or both could. He never says only one, so keep those hands busy.

The word is rejoice. "So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all." (Ecclesiastes 11:8) Every year is in there, and none gets left out. My years stuck in a junk drawer weren't the happy ones, but the years since have made up for it.

The answer is that the days of darkness will be many. "But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many." (Ecclesiastes 11:8) The Teacher doesn't pretend dark days are rare. He says to rejoice and to remember them both. Honest advice, friends.
